title: Prove batch-sensitive compiler widths and finite bit bounds
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Prove the least integer replication for fixed Theorem 1G complement and ordered-exit batches, then bound productive width and fully expanded unit-instance multiplicity without emitting the compiled word.

```text
fixed batch (rank q, multiplicity t)
  -> B_q / gcd(B_q,t)
  -> lcm over every complement and ordered exit
  -> exact B_N, P_N, O_N recurrences and rigorous bit bounds
```

The new package uses explicitly toy separated data W={3:1,4:1}, paid=(1,2,2); its general proof retains the native and whole-job hypotheses. It does not claim native admission, physical allocation, a selected-frontier change or a new κ.

## Validation

- **Before:** The pinned finite-precompilation note gives a sufficient lcm of child widths and warns that finite replication can be enormous, without a batch-sensitive size recurrence.
  **After:** The actual toy N=22 flow needs a=20 instead of uniform-width lcm 40. N=25 rejects max=16 because its necessary lcm is 80; the N=12 exit phase rejects merging repeated chronological ranks.
- Independent literal target-role flow and multinomial classes agree at every N=4,...,25. Normal and `-O` registered replay pass, including source hashes, complement integrality, paid-leaf identity, allocated-instance counts and recursive/closed bit bounds. Only standard-library Python 3.12 and bounded serial checks were used.
- Credit: Jacob Alan Sussman (Theorem 1G), zxv (higher-moment/net-tax compiler), Cinna Davis and native contributors (chronological product), Mark/Matarener (ownership audit), JoyboyBrian (source binding and this package), with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Apache-2.0.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

**Blast Radius:** isolated

Only a new research package is added. The finite calibration is toy, not an actual native supplier. Unit-instance count does not establish bank extent, precision, movement, storage bits or runtime; those contracts and the full multiplication theorem remain unverified.

## Task and overlap

Refined task `b2_math_integer_batch_growth` on card `formal-interface-lemma`; [canonical investigation](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/5062). Scientific base `4c0a359d88f22f05189d51f48387750b801a45d4`, priority revision7; refreshed canonical main is unchanged at the submission checkpoint. Exact dependency heads and retained source/path/hash records are in the scoped package. The claim states predecessor coverage, changed premise, live parallel exclusions and bounded stop rule. Arbitrary diffs and unpublished work are outside overlap coverage.

## Open next questions

See [the package questions](research/symbolic-integer-batch-width/README.md#open-next-questions) for the smallest remaining caller/interface obligation and its blocker. This contribution stops at the stated scoped result.

Reproduce with CPython3.12 on macOS arm64: `python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/symbolic-integer-batch-width`. A separate Astra review of this exact HEAD found no actionable issue and reran normal/optimized targeted checks. Scientific review remains AI-assisted, not human or proof-kernel acceptance.
